speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you've had persistent bleeding after your wisdom tooth extraction and a history of easy bruising. To understand the extent of this issue, have you noticed any other signs like frequent nosebleeds, bleeding gums while brushing, or blood in your urine or stool?

Also, have any family members experienced similar bleeding problems?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, PT, aPTT

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hematocrit: 35%, Leukocyte_Count: 8,500/mm3, Platelet_Count: 160,000/mm3; Prothrombin_Time: 15 sec; Partial_Thromboplastin_Time: 60 sec

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A (Factor VIII deficiency). The combination of spontaneous joint swelling (hemarthrosis), family history, mucocutaneous bleeding, and easy bruising is highly suggestive of a congenital factor deficiency rather than a simple acquired coagulopathy. The joint swelling indicates deep tissue bleeding, which is a hallmark of hemophilia.
